newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Eleven killed as violence surges in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Eleven killed as violence surges in Karachi.

text.p: Eleven people were killed in violence in Pakistan's volatile city of Karachi on Wednesday amid mounting tension between rival factions of an ethnic party, police and witnesses said.

Most shopping and commercial centres were shut for the second day running in a strike enforced by the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) after nine people, including five MQM workers, were shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Monday.
Police said a 15-year-old boy, Asad, was killed and three other children injured when a home-made bomb blew up in Asad's hands in Karachi's eastern Landhi district on Wednesday.
A 20-year-old worker of the rival breakaway MQM-Haqiqi, Saleem, was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in Landhi, ambulance workers said.
Another youngster, Saeed Ashraf, was killed by gunmen at the emergency ward of a government hospital in eastern Karachi.
"This surge in violence is a matter of grave concern for us," Karachi police chief Mohammad Iqbal said.
"We have set up pickets at all sensitive points, called in the reserve police and increased patrolling by police and (paramilitary) rangers in volatile parts."
Iqbal said more than a dozen workers of MQM-Haqiqi were arrested by the police on Wednesday.
Witnesses said rangers on vehicles mounted with machine-guns patrolled District Central, where the bodies of two men were found in sacks dumped in a taxi boot.
"All these killings are not political violence. There are cases in which people are settling personal scores," Iqbal said.
A youngster was shot dead in Karachi's Zaman Town area while another man was killed in a drive-by shooting at a car show room in Gulshan-i-Iqbal in the same district.
Details of the political affiliations of the victims were not given.
Police said a man slit the throat of a four-year-old boy, identified only as Arman, in Orangi Town.
Two bullet-riddled bodies of middle-aged men were found in different spots of the western district of Orangi. Both men were reported missing a day earlier.
Gunmen killed a journalist and wounded a local MQM-Haqiqi leader in the early hours of Wednesday.
The mainstream MQM's London-based leader Altaf Hussain ordered the closure of more than 100 party offices in Karachi after Monday's deadly attack on an MQM branch.
More than 100 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian unrest in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.

The MQM, long involved in a struggle with the security forces as well as with MQM-Haqiqi, was brought into a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after national and provincial elections on February 3.
